summary: Build AML streaming, feature engineering, and model-governance skills. Create practical surveillance outputs. Enquire about this course today.
lede: Real-time financial crime surveillance uses streaming data and analytics to identify and investigate suspicious activity. For AML, compliance, fraud-risk, analytics and engineering professionals, this course addresses the task of designing and assessing detection-to-investigation workflows through streaming architecture, transaction-feature engineering and model evaluation, with practice in alert prioritisation and documenting model controls.
audienceIntro: Real-time financial crime surveillance requires collaboration between compliance specialists who define risk, analytics teams who test signals, and engineering teams who make reliable data available. This course suits professionals who need to connect those responsibilities into a practical detection and investigation workflow.
prerequisites: You should have working knowledge of AML or fraud operations, transaction monitoring, risk controls, data analysis, or financial services technology. Familiarity with SQL is recommended, and basic Python knowledge will help with feature-engineering exercises, but production software development is not required. You do not need to operate a live Kafka cluster or deploy machine-learning models to production. Advanced subjects such as graph neural networks and production MLOps receive conceptual or operational coverage, while architecture mapping, feature design, model evaluation, and governance artefacts receive hands-on practice.
topics: Statistics & data analysis (SPSS, Stata, R, Python)
